question: What are two types of FC/FCoE oversubscription ratios? (Choose two.)
options: switch processing power to end-node processing power
edge ISL bandwidth to core ISL bandwidth
theory: Oversubscription in a SAN describes the ratio between the bandwidth committed on one side of a link and the bandwidth actually available on the other, and it is measured at more than one layer of the fabric: the edge-to-core ISL oversubscription ratio (aggregate host-facing edge bandwidth vs. the ISL bandwidth feeding the core) and the host-to-storage bandwidth ratio (aggregate host port bandwidth vs. available storage-array port bandwidth). Keeping these ratios low (ideally close to 1:1) reduces congestion and the risk of slow-drain conditions, while higher ratios are accepted in cost-optimized large-fabric designs. (Cisco Large SAN Design Best Practices / web research)
